text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - British stocks fell to their biggest losses in two months as bank stocks tumbled and fears grew of a possible rise in British interest rates later this week. The FTSE 100 index lost 58.5 points to 4,562.8, the biggest decline since a 65-point loss on April 1.
FRANKFURT - German stocks rose sharply, shrugging off earlier declines, with the 30-share DAX index adding 57.78 points to 3,605.62. In after-hours trading the index stood at 3,596.40.
PARIS - French shares ended higher, defying widespread expectations of a sharp drop after Sunday's Socialist election victory. The CAC-40 index rose 17.51 points to 2,601.45.

ZURICH - Swiss shares bounced back from Friday's decline as bond prices firmed and the stronger U.S. dollar also was seen as lending support. The broad Swiss Performance Index gained 63.27 points to 3,258.83.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks jumped on interest in blue-chip issues and futures though trading was light. The Nikkei average rose 383.04 points or 1.91 percent to 20,451.85.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended stronger as cash continued flowing into the market. The Hang Seng index rose 233.09 points or 1.58 percent to 14,990.90.
SYDNEY - Australian stocks also rose, hitting another record, with the All Ordinaries Index up 15.2 points to 2,625.7.

JOHANNESBURG - Big gains in industrial stocks led South African shares higher as the market ignored the impact of a nationwide strike by the country's biggest union. The industrial index jumped 50.2 points to 8,290.4 while the gold index fell 7.6 points to 1,166.6 and the overall index gained 39.6 points to 7,061.3.
